description: Provenance for the matched-condition LinearRaccess vs. Raccess Window runtime comparison (see summary.json), run to correct the confounded 'roughly 6-fold' claim in the production Fig. 3 / S3.3 comparison (unequal access_len counts K=4 vs K=1, and unequal Python-side vs. executable-only timing boundaries).
methodology_notes: Both tools are run with the same access_len list (1,3,7,10), matching the K=4 used everywhere else in this paper, rather than Raccess Window's usual K=1 (access_len=7 only) in the production benchmark/scripts/uge/raccess_w100_batch_job.sh.

Both tools are timed identically via '/usr/bin/time -v' wrapping only the binary invocation. This excludes the Python-side output validation, renaming, and SHA-256 hashing that benchmark/scripts/run_bprna_chunk.py includes inside its elapsed_sec for the production LinearRaccess runtime figure (Fig. 3A).
Both tools are run strictly sequentially (no ThreadPoolExecutor, no concurrent UGE array tasks), unlike the production pipelines which run LinearRaccess under 10-way thread-pool concurrency.

This bundle does not reproduce or replace the production 26,063-sequence Fig. 3 dataset (benchmark/results/bprna_runs/8666393, benchmark/results/raccess_w100); it is a smaller, controlled check of the constant-factor ratio only. Fig. 3's qualitative scaling-class conclusion (both linear in N, Raccess Exact cubic) is unaffected by the confounds this bundle corrects.
